paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. The LORD draws a line, and He says, "I will make a distinction between My people and your people" (Exodus 8:23). Flies fill Egypt, but Goshen gets special treatment (Exodus 8:22), and when the livestock die, not one animal belonging to the Israelites died (Exodus 9:6). He knows exactly where His people are.

Now look at Pharaoh, because he teaches us something too. Every time the pressure lifts, he goes right back to his old answer, and when the flies were gone, "Pharaoh hardened his heart this time as well" (Exodus 8:32). Then comes the hard part: "the LORD hardened Pharaoh's heart, and he would not listen to them, just as the LORD had said to Moses" (Exodus 9:12). Friend, I've said "I'll fix it tomorrow" about a leaky faucet for a WHOLE YEAR, so I can't point fingers, but this shows how a heart can dig in a little deeper each time it says no.

So what do you do with it? You trust the God who sees where you are, and you answer Him while He's still asking. The LORD's message to Pharaoh never changed: "Let My people go, so that they may worship Me" (Exodus 9:1). God wants His people free to worship Him, and He keeps His word every single time. Keep your oven ready, baker, and keep your heart soft, because this story isn't over.
